run.procedureSummary:
Start: sap 3 6 6 2 2 1 (total 20). Every segment starts QUIET. Loss tally starts at 0.
Step 1, Feed: add the cycle's feed row to segments 1 to 6. Volume is not checked yet.
Step 2, Push: go through segments 1 to 6 in order. If a segment holds more than its holding volume, cut it down to the volume and add the excess to the next segment before working on that segment, so one overflow can carry up the whole stem. Excess above segment 6 is transpired and added to the loss tally.
Step 3, Marks: for each segment, a QUIET segment with sap at or above its upper mark becomes SINK-ACTIVE. A SINK-ACTIVE segment with sap at or below its lower mark becomes QUIET. Otherwise the state does not change. Log each flip.
Step 4, Draw down: work out every amount from the sap after step 3, before anything moves. A QUIET segment respires floor(sap/4), which goes to the loss tally. A SINK-ACTIVE segment sends floor(sap/2) to the segment below it. Segment 1's send goes to the roots and into the loss tally. Then apply all amounts at once. Volume is not checked, so a segment can stay overfull.
Step 5, Leaf-drop: if the stem total is strictly over 38, set every segment to floor(sap/2). The amount removed (sap minus floor(sap/2)) is transpired and added to the loss tally. A total of exactly 38 does not fire it.
Report after cycle 5, step 5.

openPoints.point: Leaf-drop rounding with odd sap: does the segment keep the rounded-down half or lose it?
openPoints.assumption: The segment keeps floor(sap/2), and the remainder (the larger half when sap is odd) is transpired.

openPoints.point: Order of the mark checks within step 3
openPoints.assumption: Each segment is checked once, using its sap after the push and its state at the start of step 3. A segment that flips is not checked again in the same step.

openPoints.point: Draw down when one segment both sends and receives
openPoints.assumption: Every send and respire amount comes from the sap after step 3. A segment's new sap is its old sap, minus what it sends or respires, plus anything sent down from the segment above it. Amounts received are not drawn again in the same cycle.
They stay overfull until the next cycle's push (for example, segment 2 holds 10 against a volume of 8 at the end of cycle 5). The end-of-cycle-5 figures are reported overfull, as the write-up says.
It is counted in the loss tally as sent past the collar.
It fires only when the total is strictly greater than 38. Cycle 5 ended at exactly 38, so it did not fire.
